component.name: Aitch
component.summary: A text editor with nano's interaction model

description.p: Aitch is a graphical text editor that behaves the way nano does and opens folders the way an IDE does. It is modeless: you open it and you type. There is no command mode and no hidden state.

The footer is the interface. Two rows of shortcuts sit at the bottom of the window, always visible, and they change with what you are doing — they are generated from the active keymap rather than written out by hand, so they stay true even in a keymap you wrote yourself. Prompts happen on a line above them. There are no modal dialogs and no floating windows.

ul.li: Open a folder as a project, with a file tree, fuzzy file open and search across every file in it
Syntax highlighting for thirteen languages, parsed off the drawing thread so a keystroke costs the same however large the file
Files keep the encoding and line endings they arrived with
Unsaved work survives a crash and is offered back when the file is next opened
Two keymaps ship, nano and a modern one, and writing your own is the same format

screenshot.caption: Editing Rust, with the two-row shortcut footer beneath
The file tree open, and the footer showing the tree's own keys

description.p: Fixes a crash on windows wider than 2048 pixels, two ways unsaved work could be lost without being asked about, and a launch that opened an empty console beside the editor.
